subject: general
question: A ray of light is incident on a convex mirror (pole P) of radius of curvature 12 cm, parallel to its principal axis. After reflection, it appears to come from a point Q on its principal axis. Following New Cartesian Sign Convention, PQ = ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**6 cm.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given mirror is a** convex mirror,** which means it is a **diverging mirror.**
 
• The image formed by a convex mirror is always** virtual, erect, and diminished.**
 
• As the ray of light is **parallel to the principal axis,** it will reflect back through the** focus of the mirror.**
 
• This is because the **focus **of a convex mirror is situated **behind** the mirror.
 
• In the sign convention for mirrors, distances measured in the direction of incident light are taken as positive, while distances measured opposite to the incident light are negative. 
 
• Since the image is formed behind the mirror (in the direction of reflected light), the image distance (v) is considered positive. 
 
• Hence, correct answer is 6cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Increasing something's **perceived size **as opposed to its actual size is the process of **magnification.**
 
• **Optical magnification**, a size ratio, is used to quantify this enlargement.
 
• A** decrease** in size, commonly referred to as **de-magnification**, is indicated when this value is** less than one. **
